newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Five firms eye Lithuania oil terminal - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Five firms eye Lithuania oil terminal - newspaper.

text.p: Five companies expressed an interest in buying shares in Lithuania's planned Butinge oil terminal, newspaper Respublika said on Monday.

The newspaper said U.S. Fluor Daniel Inc, part of engineering and construction group Fluor Corp, Russia's oil giant Lukoil, ARA Group and Omegon Petroleum Products, submitted bids to buy into a 161.5 million litas share issue to boost the terminal's share capital to 184.7 million litas.
Butinge, in the northwest of Lithuania, has been at the planning stage for several years as the government has had troubles finding the funds for the $200 million project.
New life was breathed into the project in August when Butinge officials announce that they renegotiated the terms of an $80 million loan from the U.S. EXIM Bank.
The results of the sale of the shares to foreign firms should be announced by October 29. Foreign firms can buy up to 110 million litas of the new shares.

Butinge is part of an ambitious plan to form a new national company in Lithuania, that will comprise the terminal, the Mazheikiai oil refinery, a chain of service stations and an oil pipeline company.
